briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 8, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis: Disasters and Warnings
sections.content: In Nepal today, over 6,000 people have died or gone missing due to the devastating floods last month. The Nepalese government is demanding $20 million in climate compensation and urging major polluting nations to take action [20, 37, 43, 127, 136, 151]. International relief organization Oxfam also views the Nepal floods as a clear warning of the climate crisis and is calling for immediate climate action. Somalia is facing a severe drought crisis, while Europe has been hit by extreme heatwaves and droughts, leading to France's wine production reaching its lowest level in 70 years. Cities in the UK have been identified as most vulnerable to extreme heat [13, 18, 33, 36, 153]. Climate change is deteriorating air quality, with an increase in ultra-fine dust due to wildfires and heatwaves. In fishing grounds along the East Sea, ecological changes such as a decrease in squid and a surge in bluefin tuna are being observed [2, 9, 23]. The link between glacier collapse and climate change has been confirmed by Chinese researchers, with fatal landslides and accelerated glacier retreat occurring on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Widespread ecological disruptions have also been reported, including threatened global penguin populations and bears in Colorado breaking into vehicles due to thirst [128, 131, 142, 143, 146, 148, 149]. Economists are warning of severe economic impacts from climate change, emphasizing that humanity is in a dire predicament due to the climate crisis [141, 145].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Society: Domestic and International Efforts
sections.content: In the K-pop performance industry, a public-private-academic-industrial consultative body has been launched to establish 'Low-Carbon Performance Guidelines,' marking the first step in managing carbon emissions [45, 46, 47, 48, 53, 92, 98]. Various local governments in Korea are actively working towards carbon neutrality. Jeungpyeong-gun is offering prizes to new subscribers of its carbon neutrality points program, Uljin-gun is practicing carbon neutrality through recycling collection, and Ansan-si hosted a Citizen Environmental Festival [49, 50, 51, 54, 57, 59, 62, 65, 69, 74, 80, 81, 82, 87, 91, 93, 94]. In the National Assembly, Representative Park Jung-hyun held a discussion on 'The Green Industry Promotion System of the Carbon Neutrality Basic Act and AI Climate Tech Talent Policy Tasks,' seeking policy support. The Yongin Special City Council has embarked on discovering resource circulation policies through its 'Carbon Neutrality Research Institute IV' [75, 76, 83, 85, 86, 88, 89, 97, 99]. In the industrial sector, the transition to heat pumps in Bristol, UK, offers insights for Korea's carbon-neutral city strategies. Hyundai Motor is establishing hydrogen buses and ultra-fast charging systems in Oman, and agricultural carbon neutrality solutions utilizing genetically engineered microorganisms are also emerging [58, 64, 77, 78, 96]. Additionally, diverse everyday carbon neutrality practices are actively underway across the country, including the spread of low-carbon milk consumption, academic forums on wastewater treatment, and EM mud ball making campaigns [63, 66, 67, 68, 70, 71, 72, 73, 90, 95].

sections.title: 🌱 Integration of Renewable Energy and AI Technology: New Horizons for Energy Transition
sections.content: The Korea Energy Agency is actively supporting the overseas market entry of domestic renewable energy companies and is participating in 'Smart Energy Week 2026' in Chiba, Japan, to expand the reach of K-renewable energy [100, 103, 106, 108, 111, 112]. The role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology in responding to climate change is increasingly emphasized. The APEC Climate Center (APCC) has transferred AI climate prediction technology to the Peruvian National Meteorology and Hydrology Service, and Jeju Province is promoting an 'AI Great Transformation' and the creation of 'Energy Zero Villages' based on 100% renewable energy [24, 27, 34, 117, 118, 124, 126]. Domestic industry-academia collaboration is also active, with Kunsan National University and Korea Western Power officially commencing research cooperation in renewable energy and AI fields, emphasizing the introduction of AI prediction systems for advanced electrical safety management [101, 104, 115, 116, 119, 120, 122, 123]. The five power generation companies are set to integrate and launch as 'Korea Power' for the first time in 25 years. Challenges and solutions for energy transition are being discussed concurrently, with hydrogen gaining attention as a long-term storage alternative for the surge in surplus solar power during autumn [105, 107, 109, 110, 114, 121, 125].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Strengthening Climate Change Adaptation and Communication: Domestic and International Cooperation and Resilience
sections.content: The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) is exploring ways to deliver easier and more accurate information, such as by hosting the 'Climate Health Forum,' to enhance communication strategies regarding the health impacts of climate change [4, 19]. The Korea Forest Service held a parliamentary debate on controlling pine wilt disease and 'forest remodeling' in the era of climate change, and discussed forest ecosystem adaptation strategies, including ways to preserve and utilize Jeju's forests [3, 7, 14, 15, 16, 17, 30, 35, 44]. In the agricultural sector, Asan rice farmers are sharing their experiences and technologies for responding to climate change. However, concerns have been raised that agricultural research and development funding remains stagnant despite the deepening climate crisis, highlighting the importance of securing financial resources [28, 31, 39]. International cooperation also continues, with Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade strengthening preventive measures against climate change impacts like storms and floods, and the Global Climate and Health Alliance being awarded for mobilizing the health community in response to climate change [22, 140]. A UN report analyzes that investing $1 in climate crisis response yields an economic benefit of $15, emphasizing that climate change is a solvable crisis and conveying the message that more effort is needed [1, 8, 26, 29, 32, 41, 42, 137, 138, 139, 150].
